WhatWorked: Newer intake protocol files passed when key/hash/receipt/route/boundary/return/currentness were visible.
WhatFailed: Older history/proof/prompt-custody surfaces often lacked obvious keying, hash, return, or route joins.
WhyItMatters: The house already knows the right shape; the shape is not evenly mirrored.
RoutineUse: Use the pass files as pattern donors and the blocker-adjacent rows as repair queue, not as emergency sweep.
Boundary: Audit report is read/report only; not cleanup authority.

WhatWorked: ADOPT/ADAPT/PROOF_PARK split preserved value while avoiding raw source carry.
WhatFailed: Saving every useful idea would create bloat and false authority.
WhyItMatters: Useful source must become role-labeled candidate material with one next proof route.
RoutineUse: Each routine pass chooses one mechanism and one proof-selection route.

WhatWorked: Pattern transfer works when the assistant copies the clean concept, not the words.
WhatFailed: Rules existed but did not fire at the decision point.
WhyItMatters: A saved rule that does not fire is passive furniture.
RoutineUse: Routine must ask which rule/gate should fire before save or route changes.
Boundary: Do not scatter-fix neighboring files without proof.

WhatWorked: Saved hash points can compress live memory into current hash, receipt, active ball, next move, blocked moves, and open items.
WhatFailed: Proof history stayed live after save and made the room heavy.
WhyItMatters: History should remain retrievable without becoming the live task.
RoutineUse: Routine leaves compact pointers and drops old detail to retrieval-on-demand.

WhatWorked: One active object, one pointer, and one next condition reduce evidence saturation.
WhatFailed: More proof rows and bigger scans can replace judgment.
WhyItMatters: Clean movement needs WIP limit and currentness check.
RoutineUse: Routine starts with one selected object and stops after one next action.
Boundary: Swift Scan is support behavior, not doctrine.

WhatWorked: Helper reports improved when they named who/what/when/why/proof/boundary/stop/handoff/reopen.
WhatFailed: Helper growth reports could claim clean close while missing route evidence.
WhyItMatters: Helper files must make their usefulness assayable.
RoutineUse: Routine requires helper output contract before acceptance.

WhatWorked: Lower-layer helper failures became a scar family with shape-contract guards.
WhatFailed: Line-by-line fixes hid recurring PowerShell/report-writer shape failures.
WhyItMatters: Do not judge upper project concepts by lower-layer helper/tool failures.
RoutineUse: Routine separates upper object verdict from lower-layer repair packet.
Boundary: Does not authorize broad helper rewrite.

WhatWorked: Root material became visible through staging, tunnel, arbitration, negative-evidence, and return-trigger ledgers.
WhatFailed: Root drops had been useful but buried or easy to misread as cleanup authority.
WhyItMatters: Root/source ore needs custody without destructive movement.
RoutineUse: Routine uses root support room as example of visible parking with hash/key/map.
Boundary: No root delete, move, or doctrine adoption.

WhatWorked: Inspection-only gate gives current-state timing and repo-status signal.
WhatFailed: A due digest can become another work thread if run during dirty active work.
WhyItMatters: Routine must avoid mixing independent save threads into a dirty active pass.
RoutineUse: Park due digest as separate action unless selected; use its signal as context.
Boundary: No timer, watcher, or automatic run.

WhatWorked: Protocol-stack model correctly separates contact, identity, type, authority, transformation, join, flow, trace, helper assay, and decision.
WhatFailed: Without three-bite proof, a strong concept can overclaim readiness.
WhyItMatters: The model is right, but proof status must stay candidate.
RoutineUse: Routine uses protocol layers as silent checks and runs three-bite proof next.
